editorial_thesis: Today’s useful frontier is not another model launch: it is portable agent state, hardened self-hosting, evidence-bearing knowledge work, and task-oriented interfaces that turn capability into reviewable delivery.

topic_groups.title: Portable Agent Runtimes + Stateful Sessions
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Fresh releases point to a practical shift from single-host assistants toward sessions that survive across terminals, frontends, sandboxes, and replicas. This is an under-covered implementation lane with direct Buildn leverage.

sources.title: OpenClaw 2026.10.1
sources.why_selected: A signed Oct 10 stable release with release-evidence assets and preserved session/memory work in the project changelog.
sources.usefulness: Use as a reference for shipping update channels, evidence bundles, and recoverable agent state.

sources.title: AG-UI protocol releases
sources.why_selected: The Oct 10 ADK 0.9.0 release persists processed-message IDs across replicas; the 1.0 series tightens protocolVersion, media, approval, replay, and resume semantics.
sources.usefulness: Borrow the event-contract approach for Buildn surfaces that need a live, reviewable agent run.

sources.title: oh-my-pi 18.8.9
sources.why_selected: A fresh coding-agent release adds multiplexer-aware forking, richer session recovery, browser relay fixes, model routing, and safer shell launch confirmation.
sources.usefulness: Prototype a session handoff pattern: fork work by pane, preserve unknown outcomes, and keep browser/tool state explicit.

sources.title: GitHub dynamic workflows
sources.why_selected: Reusable sequential/parallel workflows, structured results, and human checkpoints are now shared across Copilot CLI, app, and SDK.
sources.usefulness: Model reusable Buildn jobs as declarative workflows with typed outputs and approval gates.

sources.title: Docker Sandboxes releases
sources.why_selected: Recent releases add session cleanup, long-running sandbox capability, stricter OAuth proxy handling, hostname controls, and archive limits.
sources.usefulness: Use sandbox lifecycle as the default boundary for delegated client work.

topic_groups.title: Self-Hosted AI Security + Exposure Hygiene
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Yesterday covered security verification inside delivery. Today’s fresh signal shifts outward to the infrastructure boundary: public exposure, credential mediation, and the cost of self-hosting without a hardened perimeter.

sources.title: CSA: 36,769 exposed AI endpoints
sources.why_selected: A September scan found 36,769 reachable AI-related endpoints; only 2.02% returned an HTTP authentication challenge.
sources.usefulness: Turn “private AI” into a preflight audit: bind address, auth, TLS, network policy, secrets, logs, and deletion.

sources.title: Docker Sandboxes v0.47.0 security notes
sources.why_selected: The stable release documents OAuth token interception fixes, safer hostname rules, TLS handshake limits, UDP restrictions, and kit size limits.
sources.usefulness: Create a minimal sandbox security baseline and regression checklist for agent execution.

sources.title: Microsoft Agent Governance Toolkit
sources.why_selected: The toolkit is positioned around policy enforcement, zero-trust identity, execution sandboxing, and reliability engineering for autonomous agents.
sources.usefulness: Compare its policy vocabulary with Buildn’s tool approvals, identity, and review-chain model.

sources.title: SentinelOne sovereign AI security
sources.why_selected: The announcement targets on-premise, regulated, sovereign, and air-gapped environments, including shadow-AI discovery and real-time redaction.
sources.usefulness: Use as a market signal for an AI perimeter/visibility offer rather than assuming self-hosting is automatically safe.

sources.title: GitHub third-party coding-agent validation
sources.why_selected: GitHub describes automatic security validation for code produced by supported third-party coding agents.
sources.usefulness: Pair agent identity with post-generation scanning in delegated delivery.

topic_groups.title: Agentic Work + Evidence-Bearing Knowledge
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Knowledge and learning have been under-covered recently. New research and policy signals make the useful question less “can agents act?” and more “how do we preserve evidence, skill, and human judgment while they act?”

sources.title: How agents are transforming work
sources.why_selected: OpenAI frames agents as handling longer, more complex tasks and publishes a research view of work transformation.
sources.usefulness: Use task-level decomposition in client discovery: identify the repeatable subtask, evidence needed, and human decision that remains.

sources.title: Genesis Mission + Model Hardware Standard
sources.why_selected: Anthropic describes AI-for-science support and a research preview of a Model Hardware Standard for agents operating lab instruments safely.
sources.usefulness: Translate “agent + tool standard + physical boundary” into a reusable pattern for operational systems.

sources.title: Brainrot: deskilling and addiction risks
sources.why_selected: The paper foregrounds deskilling and addiction as overlooked AI risks and discusses critical AI feedback to strengthen user memory.
sources.usefulness: Design Buildn workflows that expose reasoning checkpoints, retrieval sources, and deliberate practice instead of hiding all cognition.

sources.title: AgeMem / agentic memory search trail
sources.why_selected: Current research activity around agentic memory treats memory management as an agent policy problem rather than a passive vector store.
sources.usefulness: Test memory policies with provenance, expiry, correction, and user-visible recall controls.

sources.title: Anthropic 2026 Usage Policy update
sources.why_selected: A recent policy revision is a reminder that agent capability expansion changes the operational boundary, not just the model choice.
sources.usefulness: Make client agent proposals include an explicit allowed-use, escalation, and audit policy.

topic_groups.title: Task-Oriented AI Surfaces + Client Delivery
topic_groups.selection_rationale: The strongest product signal is moving beyond chat: reusable canvases, connected sessions, managed agents, and visual feedback loops. This lane is practical for Buildn/client work and avoids another model-launch roundup.

sources.title: When chat is the wrong UI
sources.why_selected: GitHub argues that purpose-built canvases can be faster and clearer than chat once the task is known, with bidirectional agent interaction.
sources.usefulness: Use a canvas for a client’s repeatable decision: inputs, evidence, agent action, review, and export.

sources.title: GitHub Copilot app + connected sessions
sources.why_selected: GitHub describes sessions moving across Slack, Copilot app, VS Code, and terminal while preserving context, tools, and permissions.
sources.usefulness: Design cross-surface continuity as a first-class requirement for Buildn workflows.

sources.title: Google Managed Agents
sources.why_selected: Google’s I/O materials describe Managed Agents through Interactions API/AI Studio, with named agents defined through markdown files and skills.
sources.usefulness: Compare markdown-defined agent contracts with AGENTS.md/SKILL.md-style configuration in client projects.

sources.title: Chrome DevTools MCP
sources.why_selected: Chrome exposes DevTools context to agents so rendered browser behavior can participate in inspect-debug-patch loops.
sources.usefulness: Make visual regression and runtime inspection part of agent-assisted frontend delivery.

sources.title: Figma/AI design workflow survey trail
sources.why_selected: The survey/report trail points to AI being embedded in research, ideation, and production—not merely image generation.
sources.usefulness: Package a design-to-delivery offer around context handoff, critique, and testable artifacts.
